A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEGA-Bench. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the task catalogue and error cases across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 16 VLMs, CoT comparisons, bootstrap simulations, and manual error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds model results and single-image experiments, including the demonstration-image ablation in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Appendix A introduces a limited adaptation of the benchmark query procedure: remove the demonstration image while retaining the textual one-shot example, allowing genuinely single-image queries. The taxonomy, metric suite, GPT-4o judge, answer extraction, and default prompt templates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds an input scenario in which open-source models receive only the query image, without demonstration media. This uses 273 existing Core tasks and 42 existing Open-ended tasks. The underlying 505-task, 8,186-sample corpus, domains, and detailed task catalogue remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Claude-3.5-Sonnet (1022), NVLM-72B, and Aria-MoE-25B. Appendix comparisons additionally introduce Qwen2-VL-2B, InternVL2-2B, Aquila-VL-2B-llava-qwen, two Molmo models, and POINTS-Qwen2.5-7B. This substantially expands the evaluated roster beyond v1's 16 models, including single-image-only models.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds a substantial evaluation branch using single-image tasks, CoT for Core tasks, and demonstration-image controls for open-source models; proprietary models retain demonstration images. Figure 7's bootstrap analysis switches from non-CoT to CoT responses. Section 3.1 also revises the second-round annotation target from 10 to 30 additional tasks per annotator, without establishing new data collection.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a focused ablation testing whether demonstration images help or hinder open-source models and examines performance on single-image tasks. The existing sample-count sensitivity analysis is revised to use CoT responses. The 255-task error analysis and detailed error cases are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions estimate bootstrap distributions through per-task sampling with replacement and 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Switching the analyzed responses to CoT changes the experimental condition, but not the statistical estimation procedure. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive single-image results and results for additional models. Table 2 also revises existing scores: GPT-4o's overall score changes from 54.10 to 54.21 and the original Claude model's from 51.97 to 52.13; newly evaluated Claude (1022) scores 54.27. Appendix breakdown scores also change. The PDFs do not explain the cause of the retained models' score revisions.

T1.justification: Neither version adds or changes theoretical propositions, proofs, formal assumptions, or mathematical derivations. The metric inventory remains the same; v3's explicit statement that metrics are normalized to [0,1] clarifies the existing scoring framework.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim that GPT-4o clearly leads with a near tie between Claude-3.5-Sonnet (1022) and GPT-4o, consistent with v3's Table 2. The central contributions concerning task diversity, flexible outputs, economical evaluation, and fine-grained capability reporting remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds interpretations concerning weak use of demonstration images, Gemini Flash's performance across image counts, and a tentative explanation linking NVLM's results to its training inputs. The discussion of limited multi-image ability gains experimental support for some models, extending v1's largely speculative explanation.

D1.justification: v3 adds annotator experience and task-allocation rationale, documents input-image budgets for the added models in Table 6, and describes the single-image procedure and Hugging Face Spaces leaderboard. Existing model budgets and preprocessing remain unchanged. Conversely, v1's explicit note that Open-ended demonstrations already contain CoT is omitted.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds references for newly evaluated models and VisIT-Bench. Table 1 adds SEED-Bench and VisIT-Bench, removes the GQA row, and revises several benchmark descriptions and task counts. The central positioning around broader task and output diversity remains unchanged; these overview rows are not new experimental baselines.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites portions of the construction and results discussion, combines sample-count and error analyses under Section 4.3, and inserts the single-image appendix before the retained appendices. It also adds acknowledgments and updates publication and contribution text. The overall narrative and most appendix prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the single-image comparison table, expands model and settings tables, updates Figure 5's series and legend, and redraws Figure 7's bootstrap panels. Some figures and tables shift with reflow and renumbering, while the taxonomy, prompt diagrams, task catalogue, and most case-study displays retain their designs.

improvement.justification: Appendix A tests a demonstration-image confound that v1 mainly discussed speculatively and makes evaluation possible for additional single-image models. Expanded comparisons, clearer model-version distinctions, and added settings improve usefulness and interpretation. These are incremental gains: the core benchmark remains stable, existing score revisions are unexplained, and the new overall single-image comparison uses different demonstration conditions for proprietary and open-source models.
